questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Their behaviour vexes us.

options.text: We had been vexed by their behaviour.
We are vexed by their behaviour.
We have been vexed by their behaviour.
We are being vexed by their behaviour

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**We are vexed by their behaviour**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in **Present Tense and in Active voice**.
 
• The **rule **for changing a sentence in **Present Tense** from **Active voice** to **Passive voice**:
 
 
• ​Interchange the object and the subject with each other, i.e. Object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The helping verb comes before the object in the passive voice as the passive voice starts with the object of the active voice.
 
• Convert the verb into past participle or 3rd form of the verb.
 
• **Structure: Subject + V1 + s/es + Object (Active voice)**
 
 

**​ Object + is/am/are/ + V3 + by + Subject (Passive voice)**

 
• **Solution**: *Their behaviour vexes us. (Active Voice)*

*​ We are vexed by their behaviour. (Passive Voice)*

questions.question:
Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.

When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fleed the spot

options.text: When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately flew the spot.
When the villagers putted up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fleed the spot.
When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately flown the spot.
When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fled the spot.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fled the spot.** "

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The past tense of "**flee**" is "**fled**".
 
• "**Fled**" means "**escape**".
 
 
• **Example: ***The thief **fled** from the spot when people began to crowd. *
 
 
 
• Moreover, there is no verb in English like "fleed".
 
• Therefore the appropriate option is "**When the villagers put up a firm resistance to the fearsome bandit with all their might, he ultimately fled the spot.** "

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The past tense of the verb is formed either by** adding "ed" or changing the vowel**.
 
• Not only "ed", but words ending in "e" also has its past tense by simply adding a "**-d**" and words ending in "**y**" has its past tense as"-**ied**". 
 
 
• **Example:** *cook - cook**ed**, lik**e** - like**d**, empt**y** - empt**ied**. *
 
 
 
• Some verbs **change their vowel** to get past tense.
 
 
• **Example:*** dr**i**ve - dr**o**ve,** e**at - **a**te, sw**i**m - sw**a**m. *
